test.name: Post-1850 census with shared recordArk households and a slave schedule
test.description: An 1850 census where two stubs (Edmund and Mary Dixon) share a recordArk (same household) and a slave-schedule stub appears in a separate collection. The agent should group the shared-ARK stubs into one household row, put the slave schedule in its own sub-section, and log the table as one survey_surname research-log entry with the table in notes.

input.delegation:
List every Dixon household in the Virginia 1850 census.

surname: Dixon
place: Virginia
yearSpan: 1850-1850
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged.
Should call place_search for Virginia, then record_search for 1850 only.
totalMatches is 5 (under 600 threshold), so the agent should fetch all results on one page.

Two stubs (Edmund Dixon XJQV-1850-A and Mary Dixon XJQV-1850-B) share recordArk 'ark:/61903/1:2:XJQV-HH1850-A' — they are the same household. The agent should group them into ONE household row with Edmund as head (role: Principal) and Mary as another surname member.
William Dixon (XJQV-1850-C) and James Dixon (XJQV-1850-D) each have unique recordArks — they are separate households.

Edmund Dixon (XJQV-1850-SL) is from 'United States Census (Slave Schedule), 1850' (collectionId 1420440), a non-population schedule. The agent MUST put this in its own sub-section, never merged with the population households.
The table should have two sections — one for the population census and one for the slave schedule — with Edmund+Mary grouped as one household in the population section.
Should log the search with research_log_append.

The table is logged as one research-log entry (tool survey_surname, planItemId null, query {surname, place, yearSpan}, no stagedResultsRef) whose notes hold the whole table and end with the sentence 'Censuses before 1880 have no relationship column: the first person listed in a dwelling is shown as head, and relationships are not stated.' It appears in the file changes summary as a new `log` entry; grade Table structure from that entry's notes. No file is written: the agent holds no `Write`.
The agent's return should end with the summary_for_user block.
